answer: Marble-pulse proof-of-coordination. Each epoch, the protocol samples random agent subsets; members must emit a ferrous-tagged pulse within a tight window, signed under keys derived from prior joint work. Coordinated clusters produce correlated pulse timing, which is measured as entropy collapse. Attackers running N sybils must sustain correlated timing across rounds, paying compute, latency, and marble-grade attestation costs that scale superlinearly with cluster size, since each extra identity dilutes detected entropy and forces costly desynchronization work.
